newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Harcourt in talks to buy National Education.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Harcourt in talks to buy National Education.

text.p: Publisher Harcourt General Inc., which last month launched a hostile $740 million bid for National Education Corp., on Thursday said it was in talks to acquire the company on a friendly basis for $777 million.
If successful, the move would break up a merger agreement between National Education and Sylvan Learning Systems Inc. that was struck in March.

Chestnut Hill, Mass.-based Harcourt said it was negotiating with National Education about a transaction for $21 per share, up from Harcourt's April 16 offer of $19.50 per share. It said the acquisition would be subject to due diligence reviews to be completed next week.
"If these negotiations are not successful, Harcourt General will continue its offer to purchase all NEC shares at $19.50 per share," Harcourt said in a news release.
A spokesman for Harcourt declined to discuss when negotiations had begun.
Irvine, Calif.-based National Education, which had not yet formally responded to Harcourt's initial offer, had no immediate comment.

Under the deal pending with Sylvan, shareholders of National Education would receive 0.58 share of Sylvan common stock for each share held. Orignally worth $750 million, the deal has lost value since it was announced and is now worth about $670 million.
Sylvan had little reaction to the development, saying only that it intended to proceed with its March transaction. The company would not comment on whether it would consider raising its bid.

An acquisition of National Education would extend the reach of Harcourt, known best as a traditional textbook publisher, into the growing areas of supplemental educational materials and correspondence courses.
Sylvan stock rose $1.125 to $31.25 on the Nasdaq.
National Education edged up 25 cents to $20.50, while Harcourt General dropped 50 cents to $45.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Harcourt General owns publishers Harcourt Brace & Co.; Holt, Rinehart and Winston; The Psychological Corp. and WB Saunders. It also has a 53 percent stake in the Neiman Marcus Group, which operates the upscale Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman department stores.

Baltimore-based Sylvan Learning Systems provides educational services in the United States, Canada, France, Germany and seven other countries. It has 517 franchised and company-owned learning centers, 29 public and private school-based learning centers and 14 centers at workplaces.
